labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

findings.explanation: At line 57 the p20_single_gen2 draws 8 ul from rna 1 (well A1 in slot 3) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 12 times; 96 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 12 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid. Source wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A5 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 60 the tip went into water (well A5 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 2), rt (well A2 in slot 2), dntp (well A3 in slot 2) and primers (well A4 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 12 other wells: wells A3, B3, C3, D3, E2, E3, F2, F3 and 4 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 60 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 45 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), primers, rt and 1 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 108 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: rt
findings.explanation: At line 49 the robot put rt into wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 4 (this line did it 12 times). Take well A1 in slot 4: at that moment it held only 4 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 61, to make the 9 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 4: water and buffer first, then the sample, then rt last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: rt (well A2 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 48 the tip went into rt (well A2 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 48 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
